newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P confirms rating for Westpac's Euro-MTN.
newsitem.headline: S&P confirms rating for Westpac's Euro-MTN.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said it has assigned its AA minus rating to the senior obligations and A plus to the subordinated debt under Westpac Banking Corporation's US$5.0 billion medium term note programme.
Westpac said earlier on Monday when announcing the programme that it would be rated AA-minus by S&P.

S&P said the programme would serve as Westpac's flagship Euro debt issuance vehicle and represents a key component of its strategy to establish an international and domestic wholesale funding infrastructure.
Funding proceeds from the programme would be used to satisfy general financing requirements of the bank.
"Westpac's ratings reflect its strong market position, improved asset quality, and satifactory underlying performance and capitalisation," S&P said.

S&P said that during the past three years Westpac has sufficiently revamped its management, business development, and control systems to position the bank to compete effectively in the competitive domestic market, while minimising the likelihood of high non-performing loan problems emerging in an economic downturn.
"The stable outlook reflects Standard & Poor's expectation that Westpac will remain a strong contender in the Australasian banking environment," the rating agency said.

"Like the other major banks, Westpac has a reasonably diversified product base and potential economies of scale, which should cushion it performance against over-competition in any one market segment," it added.
